items.title: Al Gallodoro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Oneonta, New York, December 28, 2005
items.q: He says, “Al I’m going to take you to this trumpet player, he’s a leader, I want him to hear you play.” And he took, me to his house and I noodled, I forget what I played, and he said, “Kid I’m going to hire you for the Forest Club.”

ctx.x: How did you get home every day from these engagements in the evening in New Orleans. Did someone have to take you back and forth or did you take a cable car?

Well yes, when I worked at the Forest Club, Howard Vorhees picked me up and took me back home. And let me tell you about that. The Coaglino family, they were in the tobacco business, and they had quite a few dollars. And Joe liked my playing. He says, “Al I’m going to take you to this trumpet player, he’s a leader, I want him to hear you play.” And he took, me to his house and I noodled, I forget what I played, and he said, “Kid I’m going to hire you for the Forest Club.” Thirty-five dollars a week, okay? That…

money. A nickel for a pack of gum, nickel for a hot dog with the sauerkraut, yeah. So anyway we’d finish the job and he’s taking me back home and he pats me and he says, “Kid, very good, I’m going to up you to fifty dollars a week.” I couldn’t believe it. This is the honest to God truth. I tell the story all the time the same. It’s not something that I put in my mind to say all the time, no, no. But my memory, I just never forgot it.
